subject: Request: trial window relief for Orbital Health — adapter sync delay
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@orbitalhealth.co>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna@orbitalhealth.co>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:04:00 -0400
Subject: Integration snag — asking for short trial window relief

Hi Priyom,

Quick note from our engineering lead: the data adapter we were integrating with your SDK is having intermittent schema errors when batching events — it's causing our end-to-end tests to fail and blocking the next set of demos. The engineers estimate 10 business days to get a stable connector (depends on a vendor patch).

We really like Redwood's perf and the team is committed, but the original trial window is about to close and we won't be able to show the 2nd demo to procurement until the connector is stable. Can we request a 3-week extension to the sandbox and an additional 3k credits to cover replays while we re-run tests?

I've attached a small integration log excerpt and the updated sprint plan.

Attachments: integration-log.txt (text), poc-schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Engineering, Orbital Health
samir@orbitalhealth.co

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@orbitalhealth.co>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 17:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Integration snag — asking for short trial window relief

Samir — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the logs. Sorry to hear about the vendor patch timeline; that's a painful blocker.

Short answer: we can help. I can provision a two-week sandbox extension today and put a provisional 2,500-credit top-up on the account while I route this for a quick approvals check. Before I finalize, two quick asks:

- Can you confirm the request owner for PO/finance follow-up (name + email)?
- Is there any data residency or new access we need to enable for the vendor patch to run?

I'll loop in Ben and Grace for approval on credits and an exception to the standard trial duration. If you need more runway than two weeks, let me know and share a concrete demo window (dates).

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: Samir Gupta <samir@orbitalhealth.co>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna@orbitalhealth.co>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Integration snag — asking for short trial window relief

Priyom — attaching the larger log excerpt you might need. Also adding more color on timelines: vendor confirmed a patch release targeted for next Wednesday (2026-05-20) but warned it could slip 48 hours. If the patch lands as planned, engineering expects two days to validate the pipeline and then we can resume demo rehearsals.

Requested: ideally a 3-week extension to cover any slip days (we'd like buffer), but we will accept a 2-week extension plus a credit top-up if approvals are easier on your side.

To confirm: PO contact is Anna Lopez (anna@orbitalhealth.co). No additional residency/access needed.

Attachments included: integration-log-extended.txt (text) — excerpt pasted below

--- begin excerpt ---
[2026-05-11 08:12:03] ERROR batch_processor: schema mismatch on field patient_id (string vs int)
[2026-05-11 08:12:04] WARN  http_client: 502 from adapter-service (retrying)
[2026-05-11 08:12:10] ERROR replay_scheduler: duplicate event id 72fa... aborting run
--- end excerpt ---

Thanks again — really appreciate the quick turnaround on this.

Samir

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@orbitalhealth.co>, Anna Lopez <anna@orbitalhealth.co>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:00:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Integration snag — asking for short trial window relief — approval request

Ben / Grace — quick request from an active PoC (Orbital Health, ORB-2147). Engineering hit a vendor adapter schema bug; vendor plans a patch next Wed (2026-05-20) with ~48h slip risk. Samir's asked for a 3-week extension and 3,000 credits; they'll accept 2 weeks + 2.5k credits as a compromise.

Why approve?
- Strong signals from product: they hit Redwood perf targets in initial runs.
- Procurement demo scheduled for the week after validation — extension materially impacts conversion timing.
- Small one-time credit reduces friction and avoids churn while vendor patch lands.

Proposed quick approval: 2-week sandbox extension + 2,500 dev credits. If you prefer, we can escalate to 3 weeks + 3,500 credits if CS wants to take on a tighter SOW. Also recommend we assign a CS engineer to do a short health-check once the patch is deployed (2h call).

Attachments: integration-log.txt, poc-schedule.xlsx (already on thread)

Appreciate a quick yes/no so I can move forward.

Thanks,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@orbitalhealth.co>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Integration snag — asking for short trial window relief — approval request

Priyom — approved. Give Orbital Health a one-time 3-week trial extension and top up 3,500 credits. We should mark this as a single exception tied to deal ORB-2147 and log the approval in HubSpot. Also please create a short CS play (2-hour validator session) and invite Grace to lead it — charge to standard PS hours if they want deeper help.

Grace — can you schedule the validator call for the week of 2026-05-25 and confirm availability?

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
